items.title: Ship one reproducible control-plane dossier for the three broken startup/saturation contracts
items.why: The canonical trace emitter promises lock inference but the canonical lock schema has no session id; session-floor returns listRemaining:null for the current valid genius cache; and brief staleness declares a 28/29 verification snapshot fresh after a direct 244/244 run because it watches only age and intent. All three are canonical Studio OS defects, so editing this repo's delegation shims would fork the control plane.
items.premise: Studio Ark can carry exact commands, exit codes, cache/lock shapes, and acceptance tests to studio-ops without a sibling-tree write. One evidence packet prevents three vague duplicate reports and gives the Mechanizer a directly executable repair recipe.
liveEvidence: skill-trace-emit start --skill studio-start exits nonzero with lock=null while context/.session-lock is valid
the lock format contains session_start but no session-id, while the canonical trace reader searches only session[-_]id
check-brief-staleness returns FRESH while STARTUP_BRIEF says 28/29 and api/build-check-diagnostics says 244/244 from this session
S291 Ark cargo 01JUDDNSAID43C1B5B481F0B03 already reports the separate static index.html sitemap false-negative
items.outcome: orientation + execution: the next /start can emit a trace, the /goal floor can name zero or the actual next item, and a warm brief cannot call stale verification live; the founder sees current evidence without this project violating CANON-018.
items.recipe: Ship a signed repo-question to studio-ops containing redacted fixtures and exact acceptance tests: trace inference accepts session_start or the lock writer adds session-id coherently; session-floor parses cache.list.items and cache.list.gated; brief staleness invalidates when build diagnostics are newer or their evidence fingerprint changes. Reference the already-open sitemap cargo rather than duplicating it.

L1.recipe: Send the three failing commands and outputs.

L2.recipe: Add minimized fixture shapes and exact acceptance criteria.

L3.recipe: Include cross-agent protocol implications, compatibility expectations, and a follow-up receipt request.

executionLog.note: Public-safe evidence and acceptance dossier shipped through Studio Ark to studio-ops as cargo 01JUILJPGC952DF42AB689BCCC; no sibling tree write.

items.title: Make closeout stamp test truth from the suite receipt instead of hand-maintained counters
items.why: PROJECT_STATUS and the closeout board still depend on an agent manually copying test counts. The existing update-test-signal helper counts only 29 top-level npm chain segments, even though the measured orchestrator owns 244 real steps, and closeout-autopilot never calls it after the blocking suite.
items.premise: api/build-check-diagnostics.json is already the public-safe source of truth with commandCount, passed, failed, and generatedAt. A pure adapter can validate that receipt and stamp PROJECT_STATUS only after closeout's direct build:check exits zero.
liveEvidence: update-test-signal.mjs derives gates by splitting package.json on && and therefore measures 29 wrappers, not 244 checks
closeout-autopilot runs build:check at Step 3e but does not update testsPassing/testsTotal afterward
items.outcome: closeout information-finding: the founder's status board and next startup snapshot show the exact verified suite cardinality and timestamp, and a malformed/red receipt fails closed instead of being copied as green.
items.recipe: Refactor update-test-signal around pure validate/apply helpers, derive only from build-check-diagnostics, add malformed/red/green self-tests, invoke it immediately after closeout Step 3e succeeds, and wire the self-test into startup smoke so the source cannot regress to top-level command counting.

L1.recipe: Read diagnostics instead of splitting package.json.

L2.recipe: Add pure validation and green/red fixtures.

L3.recipe: Wire closeout after the real suite, add a structural caller contract, and verify the rendered board source.

executionLog.note: Test signal now validates and derives exact counts from api/build-check-diagnostics.json only; closeout stamps immediately after Step 3e and reconciles derived contracts if status changes. Helper 4/4; startup smoke 60/60.

items.title: Prevent explicit external-evidence waits from entering the actionable Genius List
items.why: The current top-ranked NOW item is tagged EXTERNAL and says to act only after genuine fresh route coverage returns, yet evidenceWaitGateForTask recognizes only a narrow WAITING: REAL phrase set. The generator consequently says the item is local and unblocked, creating pressure to fabricate telemetry.
items.premise: A fail-closed evidence-wait classifier can recognize explicit EXTERNAL tags only when paired with future-observation language, preserving truly local external-integration work while gating source-of-truth waits. The same pure classifier can protect the Genius List and session-floor.
liveEvidence: .cache/genius-list.json ranks the external RUM wait actionable:true at score 96
the task text contains [EXTERNAL], after genuine fresh route coverage returns, and Do not backfill
evidenceWaitGateForTask has only two narrow regex branches
session-floor cannot currently use the cache, compounding the bad handoff
items.outcome: priority + information-finding: NOW contains work an agent can actually ship, the RUM wait remains visible with its real evidence dependency, and saturation stops on a genuinely exhausted list rather than asking for invented data.
items.recipe: Extend the pure classifier with paired external-tag/future-evidence semantics, add positive and negative fixtures for external APIs that are still locally implementable, regenerate the Genius List, and prove the RUM item moves to DEFERRED/GATED with zero actionable items.

L2.recipe: Add paired tag+future-evidence semantics and false-positive fixtures.

L3.recipe: Share the classification contract with list/floor consumers and verify regenerated human plus JSON surfaces.

executionLog.note: Classifier now gates paired [EXTERNAL] future-source evidence language; cache signature includes the classifier. Self-test 11/11; regenerated list has 0 actionable items and RUM in external-evidence-wait.

items.title: Make proof-surface diagnostics account for every command the orchestrator actually runs
items.why: check-proof-surface writes diagnostics after 66 blocking steps, then executes sixteen advisory checks outside the measured ledger. The outer build receipt reports 20.6 seconds while the proof receipt reports 16.8 seconds, and an advisory red can appear only in transient console output.
items.premise: Blocking and advisory steps can share one instrumented runner while retaining different exit semantics. The receipt can expose blockingFailed and advisoryFailed separately, preserving release behavior while eliminating invisible work and timing gaps.
liveEvidence: api/build-check-diagnostics.json measures the check-proof-surface process at 20.637s
writeDiagnostics runs before mission, CTA, public-note, identity, Oracle, Atlas, registry, Lighthouse, and duplicate-title advisories
advisory commands are spawned without rows or durations
items.outcome: diagnosis + information-finding: a maintainer can see every proof command, its duration, enforcement level, and failure owner in one committed receipt; build red remains reserved for blocking failures.
items.recipe: Introduce one instrumented runStep helper with blocking metadata, represent advisory commands declaratively, execute them before the final write, emit schema v2 blocking/advisory counts and full timings, retain warning copy, and extend --self-test to prove advisory red is recorded without failing the orchestrator.

L1.recipe: Move diagnostics after advisories and add their durations.

L2.recipe: Use one runner and separate blocking/advisory failure counts.

L3.recipe: Make advisory definitions declarative, add behavior fixtures, and verify outer/inner duration agreement.

executionLog.note: Proof diagnostics schema 2.0 records every executed command with blocking/advisory enforcement. Live: 81 commands, 66 blocking, 15 advisory, 0 failures, 18.252s measured vs 18.565s wall.
